Mal Ash helped our score along with a win in the Pole Vault with 12 feet, Harris was second in the weight, Ted Gaworski third in the Discus, Ron Liggins 6th in the Javelin, Percy Porter 5th in the Hammer - and the Sward Trophy was ours.

In Essex Percy Porter retained his Hammer title with a record throw. Many others were striving to figure in the final placings and carried the club colours creditably and we trust their day will come in the near future.

The Championships were held at Motspur Park and heats of the 440 and 880 yards, the Hammer and Javelin were held on Friday evening. In the hammer, Percy Porter went near to improving on his best performance and finished 5th with a throw of 161ft.3ins.

Jones ran exceedingly well to gain 2nd and 4th places in the sprints. Mal Ash was second in the 120 yards hurdles and Percy Porter 5th. Alan Sexton won the 440 yards hurdles in 49.7secs. a grand performance.

Thames Valley Harriers started last year a Winter Field Events Meeting and again this year put on a similar meeting. Roy Liggins, Ted Gaworski and Percy Porter competed. Percy was 2nd in the Hammer and Ted was in the first six in the Discus.

For our defence of this Trophy we were without Dick Harris and Dennis Merrett of last year's team. The first result to come through showed a fine effort by Percy Porter in the Hammer with third place.

Normally that contains a review of the season's performances and although a little late we should not forget Percy Porter's fine performances in the hammer, including a 3rd place in the A.A.A. championships and selection as an International reserve.John Powell Jones won the Welsh Shot championship a…
Although our field events representatives were few in number they certainly made their presence felt and in the very first event, the hammer throw, Percy Porter won with a throw of 157'5".

Percy Porter gave us a good start with 4th place in the hammer (155'9"), Derek McCorquindale, in his first outing for Belgrave, showed his class and won the shot with 49'0¼" and our Captain Dave Ansell took second place in the long jump with 21'4½" and, deputising for Norman Caves, 5th in the triple…

Both Percy Porter and John Ware did well in finishing 3rd and 2nd in the hammer and javelin respectively. Jim McGrath led in the long jump until the final round where two competitors"pulled one out of the bag".

In the field events D.MacCorquindale won the shot with a putt of 48'4½" , and Percy Porter was 2nd in the hammer with a throw of 157'0". Jim McGrath, who had only just overcome an injury, was fourth in the pole vault with 11'6" - a fine effort.
The field events boys were out in force and both Percy Porter and Dave Ansell won their respective events - the hammer, with 158'10½", and the long-jump with a leap of 20'5½".
Percy Porter, in the Hammer, has not reached his best but it is good to see Jock Whyte improving, winning the Middlesex only to have a bad day in the Scottish Championships.
In the hammer Percy Porter and Jock Whyte gained 3rd place and John Ware, with the ever-versatile Jim McGrath,picked up 6th place in the Javelin.

Moving from Essex to Surrey has had little effect on the performances of hammer-thrower Percy Porter. Our former Essex champion still proved too strong for the opposition and won the Surrey title with a throw of 154'-1".
